status: Native group removal, disband and logout now settle or release active loot rolls; automated checks pass; real client/network verification remains pending.
findings: RemoveMemberQueue erased the departing vote before calling CountRollVote with that same GUID. Admission immediately rejected the missing voter, so remaining completed votes and zero-voter rolls waited for the timer.
Disband cleared raw Roll pointers without completion, deletion or unblocking items; the native two-member removal path reproduced unrecoverable blocked loot.
Logout intentionally retains persistent party membership but did not remove vote participation. A pending disconnecting player delayed otherwise complete rolls.
implementation: RemoveMemberFromRolls subtracts the departing vote/counters, erases participation and calls CountTheRoll directly once remaining votes are complete. Restart iteration after vector compaction to handle simultaneous rolls.
Disband detaches player group references first, then resolves/cancels every roll while loot exists, preserving the existing eligibility checks and unblocking recovery.
LogoutPlayer removes participation from current and distinct original groups before native player teardown. Saved party membership remains intact.

native_tests.result: Both current and pinned full-game-library baseline exit 0 with empty DBErrors logs. Baseline assertions reproduce delayed completion, blocked disband item and retained logout participation; current assertions require recovery/immediate delivery.
coverage: Actual Group::RemoveMember/RemoveMemberQueue for PASS, NEED, GREED and pending departures, native refs/member slots, actual scratch SQL DELETE, two simultaneous rolls and repeated completion without duplicate delivery.
Actual two-member RemoveMember invokes native Disband and deletes/unregisters the group. Current loot remains unconsumed/unblocked and native StoreLootItem retry grants once.
Controlled quest-only roll with one eligible voter releases the item without grant when that voter leaves. Explicit FOLLOW_LOOT_RULES/non-FFA fixture is not live fragment metadata.

Actual WorldSession::Update invokes full LogoutPlayer(true), native save, map/player deletion and ObjectAccessor cleanup. Current and original-group-only variants retain three persistent member slots and the target SQL membership row, save offline state, and grant the remaining winner once. Human/orc cases use GUID104..107.
native_tests.isolation: 167 schema-only character/auth tables in two unique disposable databases, with a disposable account restricted to those schemas. World/Hotfix bootstrap remains read-only. No personal rows copied or changed; canonical config untouched. Both schemas/user removed after each run; final catalog check found zero scratch schemas/users.
native_tests.development_failures: Configured legion user could not create databases (1044), so wrapper uses admin-managed disposable schemas/user. Oversized fake names triggered native SQL1406 and were shortened; no production schema change. Shared invalid quest allocation bounds caused cleanup crashes/hangs and were corrected/revalidated in the separate fixture-integrity audit. Initial partial assertions were not accepted as passing runs.

release.binary_check: Test-GroupRollLifecycleRelease.ps1 verifies actual final-link input freshness and canonical PE bounds/thunks: RemoveMemberQueue calls cleanup, cleanup directly calls CountTheRoll, Disband calls CountTheRoll, LogoutPlayer has two cleanup calls. Prior roll/master-loot/LostArmy/Rockaway binary checks also pass.

limitations: Initial map/player/group/loot state is seeded; sessions are socketless. Native SetCanLogout gate is explicitly set before actual Update/LogoutPlayer. No actual TCP disconnect, authenticated login, World scheduler, battleground transition, LFG/leader-kick flow or saved-group reconstruction was exercised.

Test sessions are process-lifetime allocations; full Player logout/deletion is exercised, session destructor account updates are not. No real pet/client packets/loot UI or full quest completion is claimed.

Quest/conditional loot authenticity and historical client gaps from prior audits remain. This closes the controlled RemoveMember/logout lifecycle gap and does not establish complete loot-system correctness.
